patterns.name: Annual first
patterns.summary: Benefits, then the yearly and monthly plans, with the yearly plan selected and a savings badge.
structure: Yearly plan card, pre-selected, with the monthly equivalent and a savings badge
patterns.whenItWorks: Apps with steady, repeated use where a year of value is believable; when you want a longer commitment from the first purchase.
patterns.whenToAvoid: Apps with seasonal or one-off use, or when a yearly price is a shock for your audience and monthly is the real entry point.
rules: Show the real billing period and total price of the selected plan.
The savings badge must be computed from the two real prices.

patterns.name: Trial timeline
patterns.summary: Explains a free trial day by day, then asks for the purchase.
structure: Timeline: today, a reminder day, the day the charge starts
Plan and price after the trial
Cancel-anytime note that matches the store's rules
patterns.whenItWorks: Apps where the customer fears a surprise charge; apps whose value shows up within the trial.
patterns.whenToAvoid: Apps without a trial, or where the trial cannot be cancelled easily in the store.
rules: Apple 3.1.2(a): state the trial duration, what ends with it and the charge that follows, before it starts.
Show the trial only to customers eligible for the introductory offer.

patterns.whenToAvoid: Small screens with large text sizes where the hero pushes the price below the fold.
rules: Keep the price and button visible without scrolling at the largest text size you support.
Give the hero an accessibility label or mark it decorative.

patterns.name: Free versus Pro
patterns.summary: A short comparison of what the free plan and the paid plan include, then the plans.

patterns.whenToAvoid: Long feature lists: keep it to the few rows that matter.
rules: Do not hide limits of the paid plan in small print.
Use text and symbols, not colour alone, to show included or not.

patterns.name: Eligibility-aware button
patterns.summary: The button says 'Start free trial' only for customers who can still use the trial; others see the plain purchase wording.
structure: Plain price wording for the rest
patterns.whenItWorks: Any app that offers an introductory offer: Apple allows one introductory offer per subscription group per customer.
rules: Do not promise a trial to a customer who is not eligible.
Keep the plans in one subscription group.

patterns.name: Win-back offer
patterns.summary: A discounted or free period shown to a lapsed subscriber when they return.
structure: The offer and its price after the offer period
patterns.whenItWorks: Subscribers who cancelled and came back; both stores have win-back offers for lapsed subscribers.
patterns.whenToAvoid: Customers who are still subscribed, and apps that have not set up an offer in the store.
rules: Create the offer in the store first; the app only displays what the store says the customer is eligible for.

patterns.name: Billing-issue banner
patterns.summary: A banner, not a paywall, that tells a subscriber their payment failed and links to the store's fix.
structure: Banner at the top of the main screen
Button opening the store's subscription settings
Access kept during the grace period
patterns.whenItWorks: Every subscription app: the store retries failed renewals for days, and many customers never notice.
patterns.whenToAvoid: Never remove access that the store still treats as active.
rules: During a grace period the customer keeps access; Google's policy says not to remove access to content a user is entitled to.

patterns.name: Web checkout where the store allows it
patterns.summary: The purchase button opens a web checkout instead of the store sheet, for apps and regions where the store rules allow it.
structure: Button that opens the web checkout
Plain note on where the customer pays
patterns.whenItWorks: Apps in programs or regions where outside purchase links are allowed and where web pricing is a deliberate choice.
patterns.whenToAvoid: Any app where the store requires in-app purchase for the digital good. Check the current rules before shipping.
rules: Apple 3.1.1 and 3.1.3 and Google's Payments policy decide whether this is allowed for your app and country.
Re-check the rules at release time: they change.
